The Battle of Ayagoz River was a battle on the Ayagoz river between the Kazakh Khanate and the Dzungar Khanate in 1717, during the Kazakh–Dzungar Wars.
Background
The Fourth Kazakh–Dzungar war in 1708–1718 caused a dispute and destabilization between the Kazakh clans, as the Dzungars had counterattacked and recaptured lost territories in 1714. A Kazakh militia in the spring of 1717 at the district of the River Ayaguz led by Kaip and Abulkhair Khan attacked the Dzungars with 30,000 men.
Battle
.]]
The Kazakh troops, led by Kaip Khan and Abulkhair Khan, faced a well-organized Dzungar force, despite the Kazakhs’ attempts to hold their ground, the Dzungar cavalry executed flanking attacks and feigned retreats, which disrupted the Kazakh formations. On the first day of the battle, not the entire Kazakh army, but only its vanguard, was ambushed by a Dzungar border soldiers, and later on the bank of the Ayagoz River, the Dzungars fortified with using woods — effectively blocking the route to Lake Zaysan, which allowed the Dzungars to delay the Kazakhs for two days until reserves arrived. Kaip Khan had fled the battlefield but was killed at his headquarters, whilst Abulkhair also abandoned his positions and fled to Bukhara which led to the Kazakhs loosing control of Sary-Arka (except for part of the Turgay Valley). On the last day, the Dzungar force of 1,500 people defeated the Kazakhs, who, despite overwhelming superiority in numbers and in firearms, could not withstand the Dzungar's brutal penetrating strike that involved a mounted horse attack and subsequent hand-to-hand combat which caused them to retreat.
Aftermath
After the battle, The Dzungars continued their offensive with battling Kazakhs on the Arys river and at the Battle of Yuruktau, wounding Abulkhair khan in the process. The Dzungars also defeated the Kazakh troops on the banks of the Bugen, and Chayan rivers and devastated the entire South.
